newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: High-flying S.African technology sector stumbles.
newsitem.headline: High-flying S.African technology sector stumbles.

text.p: South African technology shares, for years the darlings of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), have stumbled in 1997, but analysts said on Thursday there are some buying opportunities in the sector.

The rise of the sector during the 1990s followed the trend seen on major markets like New York and London as investors woke up to the rich profits computers and information technology could reap. But the first four months of this year have seen share prices take some hard falls.

IBM South Africa Ltd traded as high as 19.75 rand on January 8, but now stands at 950 cents. Another local sector blue chip Persetel Ltd has seen its share price slump from nearly 40 rand on January 13 to around 26 rand now.

The JSE electronics index has come off a January 13 life high of 4,001 to sit at a current level of 3,329. It has been hit by twin blows of erratic moves by major technology stocks worldwide and some poor performances from local firms.

In the United States the tech-laden Nasdaq composite index has fallen around 13 percent from January 22 as a string of profit warnings from the sector hit sentiment. The bear run sparked an exit from South African technology stocks by overseas investors.
"Overseas investors have lost their nerve and pulled out of the market," said one analyst who declined to be named.
But local players have also left in droves, pushed out by bad news and pulled away by the lure of better prospects in other areas, such as telecommunications.
After a prolonged bull run profit-taking played a role.

"The problem with the sector is that a lot of people took profits and a lot of the asset allocation recommendations are that we expect better returns from some of the other sectors," said Richard Muller, analyst at SocGen Frankel Pollak.
Sentiment took a battering with poor interim results being announced by Persetel in February. In the same month IBM posted headline year earnings per share down from 69.4 cents to 55.8.
IBM compounded the gloom this month by warning it expected to show a substantial trading loss for the first half of 1997.
The despondency has left other shares in the sector hyper-sensitive to anything smacking of bad news.
On Wednesday Q Data Ltd unexpectedly said acting chairman, Piet den Boer, had resigned and would be replaced by Leen ven der Bijl. The news prompted a fall from 914 cents to touch 850 cents.
However, analysts believe the sector does offer some selective buying opportunities. Analysts said the market reaction to Q Data had been overdone and other firms also had good prospects.
"The market has totally overreacted. Q data is now a buy on weakness," Muller said.

Analysts said other major stocks like Dimension Data Ltd, newly-listed Mustek Ltd, Persetel and Q Data could also be seen as good bets, depending on the ability of their management to cope with the country's economic slow down and keep growth levels high.

Persetel has been aggressively pursuing opportunities abroad to compensate for a lack of growth at home. "Local firms are going to have to look to boost their revenue from overseas. But they are going to have to position themselves carefully...it depends a lot on the management," said one analyst.
However, firms such as IBM and Siltek Ltd would have to show better concrete earnings growth before returning to market favour, he added.
